title: Generation of a CHIP isogenic human iPSC-derived cortical neuron model for functional proteomics
protocol: Coat 12-well plates with laminin-111 according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Keep coated plates at 4°C and sterile until use.
Plate cells at a high density (80,000 cells/cm²) on Day -1 of differentiation.
Include control wells for assessment of neural induction efficiency.
Incubate iPSC with 0.5 mM EDTA diluted in PBS without calcium and magnesium for 15–20 min at 37°C until cells detach.
For each well in a 6-well plate, add 1 mL of EDTA solution.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the cells in suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend cells in differentiation media supplemented with 10 μM ROCK inhibitor Y-27632.
Plate cells at 80,000 cells/cm².
Keep cells in this supplemented media for two subsequent days.
Culture cells at 37°C in 5% (v/v) CO₂.
Reconstitute SB431542 in DMSO.
Filter-sterilize and dilute SB431542 to a 1000× working stock.
Aliquot the SB431542 stock and store at -20°C protected from light.
Thaw an aliquot of SB431542 and keep it at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
Reconstitute LDN-193189 in DMSO.
Filter-sterilize and dilute LDN-193189 to a 1000× working stock.
Aliquot the LDN-193189 stock and store at -20°C protected from light.
Thaw an aliquot of LDN-193189 and keep it at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
Remove the medium completely on Day 2.
Incubate cells with differentiation media supplemented with 10 μM SB431542 and 100 nM LDN-193189 at 37°C in 5% CO2.
For each day from Day 3 to Day 11, remove 80% of the medium carefully.
Incubate cells with differentiation media supplemented with fresh 10 μM SB431542 and 100 nM LDN-193189 at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Gently wash control cultures three times with 4°C PBS.
Use 0.5 mL of PBS per well in a 24-well plate.
Incubate cells with 4% (v/v) paraformaldehyde for 15 min at room temperature and protected from light.
Wash cells three times with 4°C PBS for 5 min at room temperature, shaking gently.
Incubate cells with blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Dilute the primary antibodies in blocking solution to the desired concentration.
Add diluted primary antibody mixture to cells and incubate overnight (16–20 h) at 4°C.
Wash cells three times with PBS containing 0.1% (v/v) Tween-20 for 5 min at room temperature, shaking gently.
Dilute fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibodies in blocking solution.
Add diluted secondary antibody mixture to cells and incubate for 1 h at room temperature, protected from light.
Wash cells three times with PBS containing 0.1% (v/v) Tween-20 for 5 min at room temperature, shaking gently.
Dilute DAPI in PBS (1:5000).
Add diluted DAPI solution to cells and incubate as required.
Add mixture to cells and incubate for 5 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Wash cells three times with PBS containing 0.1% (v/v) Tween-20 for 5 min at room temperature and shake gently.
Mount the coverslips onto microscope slides with mounting medium (VECTASHIELD® Antifade Mounting Media, H-1000, Vector Laboratories).
Remove excess mounting media.
Image cells after incubating for 24 h at 4°C.
Extract RNA using the Epicentre MasterPureTM Complete DNA and RNA Purification Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Treat extracted RNA with riboguard RNase inhibitor to prevent decay.
Treat RNA with DNase I (New England Biolabs) according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Assess the concentration and purity of the RNA.
Incubate purified RNA (1 μg) with 12 μL, 1 μL of 10 mM dNTP mix, and 1 μL of random primers at 65°C for 5 min.
Cool on ice after incubation.
Centrifuge briefly to collect solution.
Add 4 μL of 5× First strand buffer, 2 μL of 0.1 M DTT, and 1 μL riboguard RNase inhibitor.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 2 min.
Add 1 μL M-MLV reverse transcriptase or RNase-free water per sample and mix thoroughly.
Incubate samples for 10 min at room temperature.
Incubate samples for 60 min at 37°C.
Incubate samples for 10 min at 90°C to inactivate the reserve transcriptase.
Cool the cDNA mix on ice.
Add 180 μL of RNase-free water to each sample.
Snap freeze the samples.
Add 2 μL of 2 μM primer mix to each reaction.
Pipette 0.1 μL of 10 μM UPL Probe into each reaction.
Mix 5 μL of 2× UPL Probe Master Mix with the solution in each reaction.
Prepare a stock mix containing primers for multiple pluripotency and stem-renewal markers (CDK6, NANOG, OCT4) and neural progenitor markers (VIM, NES, OTX2, EMX1).
Add 7 μL of the primer mix to a single well in the 384-well plate.
Pipette 3 μL of cDNA into each well containing the primer mix.
Include wells with primers designed for detecting the housekeeping gene TATA-binding protein (TBP) on each plate.
Seal the plate and centrifuge at 67 × g for 2 minutes.
Analyze the plate using the Roche LightCycler® 480 System with Universal Probe Library (UPL).
Calculate the crossing point (Cp) value for each sample loaded per well.
Determine the average Cp of TBP expression per biological replicate.
Calculate the difference between the average Cp value of TBP and that obtained for each sample (i.e., ΔCp TBP – Cp Sample).
Assume a doubling of the target DNA during each cycle to calculate 2ˆ(ΔCp TBP – Cp Sample).
Calculate the average and standard deviations of the technical replicates per gene analyzed.
Include three technical replicates for a single biological replicate for each primer used.
Differentiate cultures with robust and homogenous expression of the neural progenitor marker Pax6 further in the differentiation protocol.
Ensure that >90% of the neuroepithelial cells express Pax6.
Verify the expression level is readily detectable by immunofluorescence assays and Western blotting.
By qRT-PCR, ensure PAX6 expression relative to TBP expression is about 6 at day 11 of differentiation.
Once cells are programmed towards a neural lineage.
Primary and secondary cortical stem and progenitor cells arise and populate the neural cultures.
Primary cortical progenitor cells characterized by Pax6+/OTX2+/Ki67+, polarization, and radial processes form rosettes visible at Day 13 of differentiation.
These primary progenitor cells give rise to secondary progenitor cells composed of two subpopulations.
Basal/intermediate progenitor cells characterized by TBR2+/Ki67+/Pax6- and the lack of basal processes arise.
Radial glial cells marked by Pax6+/TBR2- and with lengthy processes develop.
Secondary progenitor cells are present at the periphery of each rosette seen more clearly at Day 18.
Coat wells within 4-well plates with laminin-111 according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Incubate cells with 250 U/mL Collagenase Type IV diluted in HBSS containing calcium and magnesium for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash cells in wash media (1:1 DMEM/F12 and neurobasal media supplemented with 10 μM Y27632 dichloride).
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend the pellet in wash media.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend the pellet in differentiation media supplemented with 10 μM Y27632 dichloride, 100 nM LDN and 10 μM SB431542.
Plate cells at a 1:1.5 ratio.
Incubate cells for 24 hours before replacing the differentiation media.
Renew differentiation media daily or every two days as needed.
Incubate cells with 250 U/mL Collagenase Type IV diluted in HBSS containing calcium and magnesium for 30 min at 37°C.
Triturate the cells by pipetting several times (with 1 mL pipette tips).
Wash cells in wash media (1:1 DMEM/F12 and neurobasal media supplemented with 10 μM Y27632 dichloride).
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend the pellet in wash media.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend the pellet in differentiation media supplemented with 10 μM Y27632 dichloride.
Plate cells at a 1:2 ratio.
After 24 h, remove all the media and incubate cells with differentiation media only.
Renew the differentiation media daily or every 2 days, depending on the need.
Passage neural stem cells on Day 25 of the differentiation.
Pre-coat 4-well plates with poly-L-ornithine according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Day 23 of the differentiation).
Coat the pre-coated 4-well plates with laminin-111 according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Day 24 of the differentiation).
Incubate cells with Accutase for 10–15 min at 37°C.
Triturate cells by pipetting several times until dissociated into single cells.
Add wash media.
Filter cells in suspension using a 40 μm cell strainer to remove aggregates.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 180 g.
Resuspend cells in differentiation media supplemented with 10 μM Y27632 dichloride.
Plate cells at a low density (35,000 cells/cm²) or high density (80,000 cells/cm²).
Remove the media completely after 24 h.
Incubate the cells with differentiation media supplemented with 20 ng/mL BDNF and 20 ng/mL GDNF.
Replace half of the media with fresh differentiation media supplemented with 20 ng/mL BDNF and 20 ng/mL GDNF from Day 26 to 80 of the differentiation protocol.
Observe cultures routinely to detect early signs of proliferating contaminating cells.
Assess the expression of FOXG1 and TBR2 markers during cortical neurogenesis.
Evaluate the increase in TBR1 and CTIP2 markers for early-born deep-layer neurons.
Analyze CUX1 and BRN2 marker expression for late-born upper-layer neurons.
Conduct immunofluorescence analysis at Day 50 and Day 80 to assess early-born upper-layer neuronal markers.
Quantify the percentage of neurons that are TBR1-/CTIP2+, TBR1+/CTIP2-, and TBR1+/CTIP+.
Assess the expression of CUX1 marker at Day 80 for late-born upper-layer neurons.
Conduct an immunofluorescence assay targeting β(III)-tubulin to assess neuronal network complexity.
Analyze markers of secondary progenitor cells, early-born upper-layer neurons, and late-born deep-layer neurons by qRT-PCR.
Conduct qRT-PCR analysis on Days 0, 11, 25, 45, and 80 during differentiation to assess expression profiles.
Target FOXG1 primers to monitor secondary progenitors development.
Use TBR1 and CTIP2 primers to identify early-born deep-layer neurons.
Employ CUX1 and BRN2 primers for late-born upper-layer neuron monitoring.
Reconstitute cell lines in 8 M Urea buffer for lysing.
Proteolytically digest extracted proteins into tryptic peptides compatible with bottom-up mass spectrometry.
Carry out trypsinization on 10 kDa filters for Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP).
Reduce disulfide bridges of the lysate to disrupt protein tertiary structure.
Alkylate free sulfhydryl groups after reduction.
Digest proteins efficiently using protease due to accessible cleavage sites.
Desalt resultant peptides on C18 columns.
Dry desalted peptides by evaporation.
Wash neuronal cultures twice with 4°C PBS at day 80 of differentiation.
Add lysis buffer to each well and incubate for 30 minutes on a shaking table.
Transfer the lysate to an Eppendorf tube after incubation.
Centrifuge samples at 14,000 × g for 20 minutes, 8°C.
Transfer supernatant to new labeled tubes.
Measure the protein concentration using micro-BCA following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Snap freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen and store at −80°C.
Mix 100 μg of protein extract (in up to 30 μL volume) with 200 μL urea buffer on the filter.
Centrifuge the Microcon unit at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 20°C.
Add 200 μL of urea buffer to the filter and repeat the centrifugation.
Discard the flow-through.
Mix 100 μg of protein extract with 100 μL urea buffer containing 100 mM Tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine hydrochloride pH 8.5.
Incubate the unit in a thermomixer at 600 rpm for 30 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge the filter unit at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 20°C.
Mix 100 μg of protein extract with 100 μL urea buffer containing 50 mM iodoacetamide pH 8.5.
Incubate the unit without shaking in the dark for 20 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge the filter unit at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 20°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Mix 100 μg of protein extract with 100 μL 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate pH 7.8.
Centrifuge the filter unit at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 20°C.
Repeat the previous step twice.
Transfer the filter unit to a new collection tube.
Add 100 μL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate pH 7.8 to the sample.
Pipette sequencing grade modified trypsin at an enzyme-to-protein ratio of 1:50 (w/w) into the mixture.
Incubate the unit in a thermomixer at 600 rpm for 60 minutes at 37°C.
Continue incubation overnight (16–20 hours) at 37°C in a humid chamber.
Centrifuge the filter unit at 14,000 × g for 15 minutes at 20°C to elute peptides through the filter membrane.
Measure the peptide concentration using the Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dry the sample in a SpeedVac with thermostat set to 37°C until all liquid evaporates.
Dissolve the evaporated sample in 100 μL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid using a bath sonicor for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash Micro Spin C-18 Columns with 200 μL of 100% (v/v) acetonitrile containing 0.1% (v/v) formic acid.
Centrifuge at 100 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Repeat the wash steps three times and discard the flow-through from the collection tube.
Wash the columns with 200 μL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid (aqueous).
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Add 200 μL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and hydrate the column for 15 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at room temperature and discard the flow-through from the collection tube.
Check the pH of the sample; it must be acidic.
Load the sample onto the column and centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Wash the column three times with 200 μL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid followed by centrifugation at 500 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer the column to a new collection tube prior to peptide elution.
Add 200 μL of 20% (v/v) acetonitrile with 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Add 200 μL of 40% (v/v) acetonitrile with 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Add 200 μL of 60% (v/v) acetonitrile with 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and centrifuge at 500 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer all fractions containing the eluted peptides to new eppendorf tubes.
Dry the samples by evaporation in a SpeedVac set to 37°C until completely evaporated.
Store the sample at -20°C for short-term storage.
Store the sample at -80°C for long-term storage.
Use glass pipettes or Hamilton syringes when transferring acids >2% concentration.
Prepare solutions fresh in glass bottles.
Perform label-free quantitative comparison of proteomes using SWATH-MS method.
Measure the same sample set in a data-dependent manner (DDA/shotgun proteomics) to create a spectral library.
Extract data from SWATH mass spectrometry to provide quantitative information on proteins expressed in two different states.
Add 100 μL of 5% (v/v) acetonitrile (ACN) and 0.05% (v/v) trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).
Vortex the mixture for 30 seconds.
Sonicate the mixture using a sonicating water bath for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 10,000 g for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant into a clear vial.
Determine the absorbance of the dissolved peptide samples at 220 nm and 280 nm.
Inject 1 μL of the most concentrated sample and the least concentrated sample into the LC-MS/MS system in data-dependent mode.
Check intensities and profiles of total ion currents to ensure they resemble cell line peptide digest profiles and no contaminants are present.
Determine the number of identifications, ensuring at least 1,000 proteins are identified with a false discovery rate less than 1%.
Use absorbance values at 220 nm and 280 nm to set sample injection volumes for maximum allowed full mass spectrometric intensity.
Utilize these absorbance values to dilute the samples in order to load approximately 2 μg of peptides in a column injection volume of 3.7 μL.
Pool replicates from knockout and wild-type cell lines equimolarly to prepare a spectral library of pooled samples.
Inject approximately 2 μg of pooled peptides onto a Eksigent Ekspert nanoLC 400 connected to a TripleTOF 5600+ mass spectrometer.
Pre-concentrate the sample on a cartridge trap column using a mobile phase composed of 0.05% trifluoroacetic acid in 2% (v/v) ACN.
Separate pre-concentrated peptides analytically on a capillary column packed with C18 PepMap100 sorbent, 2 μm particle size.
Start the analytical gradient from 2% B and increase linearly to 40% B in 120 min at a flow rate of 300 nl/min.
Ionize the analytes by a nano-electrospray ion source with drying gas temperature set to 150°C and flow rate set to 12 psi.
Set the capillary emitter voltage to 2.65 kV.
Measure the spectral library using the DDA method with a precursor range from 400 Th up to 1250 Th.
Fragment product ions within a range of 200 Th up to 1600 Th during each cycle.
Set cycle time to 2.3 s, fragmenting the top 20 most intensive precursor ions per cycle.
Set the precursor exclusion time to 12 s.
Search data derived from DDA against a Homo sapiens reference database using ProteinPilot 4.5.
Set trypsin as the protease and carbamidomethyl moiety as a fixed modification.
Set the tolerated mass error in MS1 and MS2 to predefined TripleTOF 5600 settings.
Perform FDR calculation by searching DDA MS/MS data against decoy entries.
Acquire SWATH data by injecting approximately 2 μg of three biological replicates of peptide samples from knockout and wild type cell lines, each measured in technical triplicate.
Perform liquid chromatography under completely identical chromatography conditions as described for the spectral library.
Acquire SWATH data in high sensitivity positive mode.
Set precursor range from 400 Th up to 1200 Th and divide into 67 precursor SWATH windows with a 12 Th width and 1 Th overlap.
Set accumulation per SWATH window to 50.9 ms resulting in a 3.5 s cycle time.
Scan product ions in a range from 360 Th to 1360 Th.
Use rolling collision energy setting with 15 mV collision energy spread.
Extract quantitative proteomic data from SWATH-derived spectral data.
Quantify protein quantities and statistically compare between conditions using extracted data.
Identify significantly associated Gene Ontology (GO) terms using bioinformatic analysis tools.
Graphically represent GO terms using DAVID software.
Conduct pathway analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA).
Include a maximum of 4 peptides per protein in the spectral library.
Include 6 product ions per peptide in the spectral library.
Analyze proteins using SWATH™ Acquisition MicroApp 1.0 plugin applied to PeakView 1.2.0.3.
Determine retention time window based on variability in the dataset.
Set retention time extraction window width to ±4 min around the expected retention time.
Set product ion chromatogram extraction mass accuracy as ± 0.05 Da around the expected product ion mass.
Use extracted product ion chromatograms to determine peak areas for each transition in MarkerView software.
Use extracted transition intensities to calculate protein and peptide levels in MarkerView software.
Perform a t-test on quantitative data from wild type and knockout cell lines to determine significantly altered steady-state protein levels (p>0.01).
Use a Benjamini-Hochberg test to adjust p-values.
Convert protein identifiers to gene symbols for GO term analysis using GOrilla.
Choose Homo sapiens as the organism of interest in GOrilla.
Include all proteins with fold changes ≤0.67 and ≥1.5 in the target set for GO term analysis.
Include all proteins with fold changes ≤0.67 and ≥1.5 along with their exact fold changes.
Select Homo sapiens as the organism and “Official_Gene_Symbol” as the identifier for the gene list.
Derive different categories of GO terms, including molecular function and biological process.
Derive pathways, including KEGG pathways.
For each GO term/pathway, provide the number of entries from the input list that are involved in a term ("count").
Present gene-enrichment analysis as a Modified Fisher Exact p-value ranging from 0 to 1 (“p-value”).
Provide an adjusted p-value using Benjamini (“Benjamini”) for enrichment analysis.
Use REVIGO software to plot GO terms and pathway analysis results, with GO terms color-coded based on their Log10(p-value).
Only significantly enrich GO terms (q val > 0.05) are plotted in the graphical representation.
Predict changes in canonical pathways and potential upstream regulators using IPA software.
Upload protein data with fold changes and p-values to IPA for pathway analysis prediction.
When focusing on membrane proteins, sort them using IPA software.
Use a cut off of -log(p-value) > 1.3 (corresponding to p-values <0.05) for the analysis.
